data.author: Mera Aladam

Why is Turkey warning of an Israeli military operation in Syria?
Turkey's foreign minister has warned that Israel could launch a military operation in Syria, accusing it of backing a faction within the country's Druze community in an attempt to provoke the Syrian army and create a pretext for intervention.
Hakan Fidan made the remarks in a televised interview with Turkish broadcaster TGRT Haber on Saturday, saying Ankara had raised the possibility with regional allies, as well as US and European officials.
"There is a scenario in which the Israeli army uses this as a pretext to launch an operation against Syria," Fidan said.
The Turkish foreign minister also alleged that Israel was supporting one of three major factions within Syria's Druze community, supplying it with weapons and ammunition by helicopter on a weekly basis.

data.title: Middle East Eye: From arson to land seizures: Settlers tighten grip on Palestinian villages near Ramallah
data.author: Mera Aladam
data.summary:
From arson to land seizures: Settlers tighten grip on Palestinian villages near Ramallah
In a series of coordinated attacks across several villages near the city of Ramallah in the central occupied West Bank, Israeli settlers torched Palestinian vehicles between Saturday evening and Sunday morning.
The settlers also spray-painted racist slogans on the walls of homes in the three villages, calling for the killing of Arabs and for revenge against them.
Rafat Abu Musa, head of the village council of Deir al-Sudan, north of Ramallah, told Middle East Eye that settlers infiltrated the southern part of the village at 11.30pm on Saturday and set fire to two vehicles.
They spray-painted slogans in Hebrew on the walls of nearby houses, he said, adding that the same area had been targeted by a similar attack two months ago, during which a vehicle was set on fire.
Abu Musa indicated that the settlers came from a newly built outpost on the summit of Jabal al-Ras, located in the neighbouring village of Umm Safa.

data.author: Mera Aladam
data.summary:
Trump claims he predicted drops in oil prices, stock market and hits from Iran after Democratic win in midterm elections
US President Donald Trump claimed that he predicted a stock market decline as well as harsher attacks from Iran after the Democratic Party's victory in the recent midterm elections.
"As everyone remembers, I predicted two things concerning the November 3rd Midterm Elections. One, that if the Democrats win, the Stock Markets would go down, substantially, which they have, and two, that the Islamic Republic of Iran... will grow more aggressive in their attacks, which has also occurred," he wrote in a post on his social media platform Truth Social.
Trump added that Iran "launched more drones and missiles in the last week than at any time for over a year", but claimed that the attacks have "all been knocked down, and done no damage".
"Iranian leaders consider the Democrats weak, ineffective, and Country destroying, but I won’t let that happen! Both the Dems and Iran fought like hell to keep the Oil price up as long as possible and, since the Election, the Oil price has dropped by a record level," the American president further claimed.
Trump went onto describe the elections as "very strange".
In another post, he questioned the drop in oil prices, saying: "Isn’t it interesting that Oil prices have dropped precipitously after the Midterm Elections? I said that was going to happen. The whole thing is a Giant Hoax!"

data.title: Middle East Eye: Opinion: Anti-Muslim racism is a global system used to normalise mass killing
data.author: Mera Aladam
data.summary:
Opinion: Anti-Muslim racism is a global system used to normalise mass killing
Dr Amina Shareef, a researcher of anti-Muslim racism, says that the destruction unfolding in Gaza, Iran and Lebanon is part of a longer history of anti-Muslim racism that has made mass Muslim suffering and death politically permissible.
She says that Islamophobia is not simply a matter of prejudice or discrimination, but a global system of racial power that constructs Muslims and those identified as Muslim as security threats, allowing violence against them to be justified in the name of security.
Central to this system is the figure of the Muslim terrorist, which portrays Muslim political agency as inherently threatening. Shareef says that this logic extends beyond surveillance, detention and militarised borders to warfare, political abandonment and the destruction of the conditions necessary for life.
She identifies Palestine as a key site where contemporary security practices and technologies of control have been refined and reproduced elsewhere, a process she describes through the concept of the “Palestine boomerang”. Although conflicts in Iran, Lebanon, Kashmir, Syria, Yemen, Iraq and Afghanistan have distinct histories, she argues that they reveal a recurring pattern in which Muslim populations are portrayed as threats and their suffering becomes easier to justify.
Shareef concludes that confronting anti-Muslim racism is ultimately a struggle to protect life and human dignity. She calls for sustained resistance to systems that expose entire populations to premature death, arguing that the responsibility to seek justice remains even when the outcome is uncertain.

data.author: Tarek Yousef Tahan
data.summary:
Meet the Pacific Islanders standing for Palestine against Christian Zionism
Submitted by
Tarek Yousef Tahan
on
Mon, 11/23/2026 - 11:00
In Fiji, Samoa and other islands, deep-rooted evangelical Zionism is being challenged
Mara Mahoney, Michel Mulipola and James Bhagwan are all standing in solidarity with Palestinians across the Pacific Islands (Supplied/MEE)
Off
Michel Mulipola is a comic book artist and former professional wrestler. He’s also an activist for indigenous self-determination in Palestine and across the Pacific Islands, as well as a former Green Party candidate in New Zealand.
It’s in keeping with his family history. Mulipola’s great-grandfather, Mataʻutia Karauna Solomona, was a Samoan resistance leader and secretary of the Mau movement, which sought to free Western Samoa of colonial rule in the 1920s and 1930s.
Solomona’s arrest resulted in a massacre of unarmed protesters by the New Zealand military and police.
“So, I guess activism or even just fighting for freedom, for sovereignty, is in my blood,” says Mulipola, who has received media attention for his customised image of the Palestinian flag using traditional Samoan petroglyphs.
The artwork, which incorporates symbols drawn from Samoan cultural traditions, became a way for Mulipola to explain why he believed his people should stand with Palestinians.
Samoans around the world grew more curious, and have carried the flag at Palestine demonstrations. But the response was not all positive.
“Christian Zionism has got quite a strong stranglehold on Samoans and other people of the Pacific,” Mulipola tells Middle East Eye in a video call interview.
A self-described atheist, Mulipola was accused of not being truly Samoan, just because he did not support Israel.
'Christian Zionism has got quite a strong stranglehold on Samoans and other people of the Pacific'
- Michel Mulipola, comic book artist and activist
These reactions exposed a deeper tension present in the Pacific islands since even before the start

data.title: Middle East Eye: Israeli strike kills Unrwa worker in Gaza, the UN Palestinian agency says
data.author: Alex MacDonald
data.summary:
Israeli strike kills Unrwa worker in Gaza, the UN Palestinian agency says
An Israeli air strike killed a man working for the UN Palestinian refugee agency Unrwa in the Gaza Strip on Monday, the relief agency and local health officials said.
The Palestinian man, whom medics named as Adel al-Helo, was working near a water well in the Jabalia refugee camp in the enclave's north, Unrwa and medics said. Three others were wounded in the strike, they said.
"The initial reports indicate that the strike hit a target on the street near the water well, which was manned by Unrwa staff and a guard. The staff were engaged in their regular duties associated with water well operations," an Unrwa spokesperson told Reuters.
Reporting by Reuters
